evals.prompt: Do an architectural and competitive deep-dive on Qualified PiperX vs Drift. Seed URLs: https://www.qualified.com/platform, https://www.drift.com/platform. I need this for a CPO presentation next week.
evals.expected_output: A full 7-section deep product analysis report covering both Qualified and Drift. An Executive Summary of 4-8 bullets appears before Section 1. Section 1 includes ICP and Anti-ICP analysis for both products. Section 2 uses the 3-layer framework with evidence classification (verified/inferred/strategic interpretation) applied to architectural claims. Section 3 walkthrough notes which steps are documented vs. inferred, with an Agent Operating Model sub-section for Qualified PiperX. Feature matrix covers both companies. Section 5 migration ratings are anchored to observable dependencies. Section 6 roadmap threats are classified by signal type. Citations Appendix is populated.

assertions.name: all_7_sections_present
assertions.description: The report contains all 7 numbered sections: (1) Strategic Overview & Archetype, (2) Architectural Blueprint & AI Governance, (3) How It Works, (4) Scalable Feature Matrix, (5) Switching Costs & Integration Tax, (6) Roadmap Threat & PM Recommendation, (7) Citations Appendix

assertions.name: executive_summary_always_present
assertions.description: An Executive Summary of 4-8 bullets appears before Section 1. It covers: core takeaway, where each company wins (one phrase per company), biggest strategic risk with signal type noted, and a recommendation.

assertions.name: citations_appendix_populated
assertions.description: Section 7 (Citations Appendix) exists and contains at least one URL per company (Qualified and Drift), with source types noted

assertions.name: feature_matrix_covers_all_companies
assertions.description: The feature comparison matrix in Section 4 contains columns for both Qualified and Drift

assertions.name: fact_inference_separation
assertions.description: Section 2 and Section 3 distinguish between verified documented facts and inferred architectural behaviors. Claims about internal implementation (e.g., exact CRM object behavior, model internals, exact API sequences) use hedged language ('appears to', 'based on documented behavior', 'inferred') rather than stating them as verified facts. The report does not present inference as documentation.

assertions.name: no_overclaimed_internal_architecture
assertions.description: The report does not state specific internal implementation details — such as exact Salesforce custom object names or schemas, internal AI model identities, exact data pipeline sequences, or specific API field names — as verified facts without a cited source. Where such details are not publicly documented, the report uses 'Proprietary / Not Publicly Disclosed' or explicitly frames the claim as inferred.

assertions.name: evidence_calibration_on_sensitive_claims
assertions.description: Sensitive claims — including compliance certifications (SOC 2, GDPR posture), training data privacy policies, exact pricing figures, and migration timeline estimates — are either sourced with a specific citation or appropriately hedged. No compliance or privacy claim is stated as fact based solely on vendor category norms or enterprise customer presence.

assertions.name: executive_readability
assertions.description: Each major section and company block in Section 2 leads with a Headline Takeaway (1-2 sentences stating the strategic 'so what') before the technical detail. The report is scannable: a CPO could extract the key implications without reading every sub-bullet.

assertions.name: defensible_roadmap_threat
assertions.description: Each roadmap threat in Section 6 is classified by signal type: [Shipped], [Announced], [Signal-based], or [Strategic Interpretation]. No threat is presented with higher confidence than its evidence warrants. The classification is explicit in the text, not implicit.

assertions.name: agent_capability_model_coverage
assertions.description: Qualified PiperX is positioned as an AI SDR agent. The report must explicitly name Piper's major capability surfaces (e.g., web chat, email, meetings, offers, nurture) as distinct items — not collapse them into 'pipeline generation' or 'conversion.' The report must describe how those capabilities connect into an operating loop, identify which are central vs. ancillary, and state the autonomy boundary (what Piper does autonomously vs. what requires human initiation or handoff). This appears as an 'Agent Operating Model' sub-section in Section 3.
